arxiv-2008-07161.title: Spectrum and Analytic Functional Calculus for Clifford Operators via Stem Functions
arxiv-2008-07161.creator: Florian-Horia Vasilescu
arxiv-2008-07161.description: Abstract The main purpose of this work is the construction of an analytic functional calculus for Clifford operators, which are operators acting on certain modules over Clifford algebras. Unlike in some preceding works by other authors, we use a spectrum defined in the complex plane, and certain stem functions, analytic in neighborhoods of such a spectrum.

arxiv-2103-15599.title: Graph-based Facial Affect Analysis: A Review
arxiv-2103-15599.creator: Yang Liu, Xingming Zhang, Yante Li, Jinzhao Zhou, Xin Li, and Guoying Zhao
arxiv-2103-15599.description: Abstract As one of the most important affective signals, facial affect analysis (FAA) is essential for developing human-computer interaction systems. Early methods focus on extracting appearance and geometry features associated with human affects while ignoring the latent semantic information among individual facial changes, leading to limited performance and generalization.

arxiv-2112-14679.title: Profile Guided Optimization without Profiles: A Machine Learning Approach
arxiv-2112-14679.creator: Nadav Rotem, Chris Cummins
arxiv-2112-14679.description: Abstract Profile guided optimization is an effective technique for improving the optimization ability of compilers based on dynamic behavior, but collecting profile data is expensive, cumbersome, and requires regular updating to remain fresh. We present a novel statistical approach to inferring branch probabilities that improves the performance of programs that are compiled without profile guided optimizations.

arxiv-2207-11523.title: Unstructured Road Segmentation using Hypercolumn based Random Forests of Local experts
arxiv-2207-11523.creator: Prassanna Ganesh Ravishankar, Antonio M. Lopez, Gemma M. Sanchez
arxiv-2207-11523.description: Abstract Monocular vision based road detection methods are mostly based on machine learning methods, relying on classification and feature extraction accuracy, and suffer from appearance, illumination and weather changes. Traditional methods introduce the predictions into conditional random fields or markov random fields models to improve the intermediate predictions based on structure.

arxiv-2212-04127.title: Progressive Multi-resolution Loss for Crowd Counting
arxiv-2212-04127.creator: Ziheng Yan, Yuankai Qi, Guorong Li, Xinyan Liu, Weigang Zhang, Qingming Huang, Ming-Hsuan Yang
arxiv-2212-04127.description: Abstract Crowd counting is usually handled in a density map regression fashion, which is supervised via a L2 loss between the predicted density map and ground truth. To effectively regulate models, various improved L2 loss functions have been proposed to find a better correspondence between predicted density and annotation positions.

However, such emotional aspects are often ignored by current platforms, which affects the listeners’ ability to find music that triggers specific personal feelings.

pmc-12751217.description: BackgroundT cells play a pivotal role in the autoimmune destruction of beta cells in type 1 diabetes. However, our understanding of the disease has been limited by lack of a comprehensive single-cell transcriptome analysis of T cells during its early stages.
